title: ad-hoc-eval-scratchpad-regression-hypotheses
content:
Quick log: informal running notes on a small regression I noticed after model roll (v2.3 -> v2.4) on hosted-api. Trying to capture hypotheses and cheap experiments before I forget.

Context:
- Surface: chat/text generation endpoint used by onboarding helper (short Q/A, strict JSON output expected).
- Observed change window: between 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-03 deployments (customer traffic + synthetic tests).
- Symptoms: slightly higher hallucination rate on entity facts, more dropped fields in structured outputs, and occasional extra commentary appended after the JSON blob (formatting regression).

Ad-hoc rubric (0..3, 3 = good):
- Correctness (factual): 0/1/2/3 -> marking obvious factual errors
- Format compliance (strict JSON): 0/1/2/3 -> 3 = exactly valid JSON only, 2 = JSON plus benign whitespace, 1 = JSON with trailing commentary, 0 = missing or malformed
- Conciseness / verbosity: 0..3 -> penalize extra filler text added
- Hallucination (invented entities): 0..3 -> 3 = none seen, 0 = frequent wrong facts
- Safety / toxic content: 0..3 -> quick sanity check

Scoring notes: run 50 samples per prompt, compute proportion of responses with format compliance >=2 and hallucination >=2. For quick manual triage, I sampled 8 prompts below.

Sample prompts (short form):
P1: "Summarize the onboarding steps for an enterprise user in JSON with keys: steps, approx_time_minutes"
P2: "Given user email b@example.com, return JSON {valid_email: true/false, domain: <domain>}"
P3: "List 3 known limitations of model X (verifiable facts). Output JSON array of strings."
P4: "Extract {name, company, location} from the following message: 'Hi, I'm Sam from Acme Corp, SF.'"

Observed outputs (v2.3 baseline vs v2.4 current) — representative samples (manually trimmed):
- P1 baseline (v2.3): "{\"steps\": [\"create org account\", \"invite team\"], \"approx_time_minutes\": 45}"  -> rubric: correctness 3, format 3, verbosity 3, hallucination 3
- P1 current (v2.4): "{\"steps\": [\"create org account\", \"invite team\"], \"approx_time_minutes\": 45} Also note: make sure to check billing settings." -> rubric: correctness 3, format 1 (trailing commentary), verbosity 1, hallucination 3

- P3 baseline (v2.3): "[\"limited context window (16k)\", \"occasional factual drift after 1000 tokens\", \"sensitivity to prompt phrasing\"]" -> format 3, correctness 2
- P3 current (v2.4): "[\"limited context window (16k)\", \"occasional factual drift after 1000 tokens\", \"sensitivity to prompt phrasing\"]\nNote: also depends on model quantization." -> format 1, verbosity 1

- P4 baseline: "{\"name\": \"Sam\", \"company\": \"Acme Corp\", \"location\": \"SF\"}" -> format 3
- P4 current: "{\"name\": \"Sam\", \"company\": \"Acme Corp\"}" (location missing) -> format 3 but correctness 1 (dropped field)

Initial quantification (quick):
- Format compliance (format >=2): baseline 98% (n=50), current 74% (n=50)
- Hallucination (hallucination >=2): baseline 92%, current 87% (small drop)
- Field-completeness for extraction tasks: baseline 96%, current 78%

Preliminary hypotheses (ordered):
1) Prompt-handling change: a new normalization step in routing or tokenization adds a trailing system/assistant note being appended during streaming flush. Check streaming vs non-streaming responses.
2) Decoding / temperature defaults changed in rollout config (e.g., top-p or repetition penalty). That could explain extra commentary or dropped short fields if early stopping triggered.
3) New kernel/quantization path in v2.4 triggers slightly different tokenization boundaries, causing the model to produce safe follow-up commentary appended to the JSON (post-hoc safety wrapper).
4) A guardrail microservice (post-processing) added at the edge to append clarifying text when response length > X. Need to check infra diffs.
5) Query routing to a newer variant with a different system prompt (weaker format enforcement).

Quick experiments to run (cheap, measurable):
- R1: Re-run failing prompts with ?stream=false vs true on the same model/commit; capture raw tokens. Compare where the commentary is produced (during or after JSON).
- R2: Call dedicated instance pinned to v2.3 artifact and compare to v2.4 hosted; isolate whether it's model artifact or platform change.
- R3: Insert explicit instruction in prompt wrapper ("OUTPUT_ONLY_JSON: true") and see if format compliance recovers; this tells if it's model-level instruction tuning change.
- R4: Re-run with quantization disabled (if available) and compare completions; helps confirm kernel/quantization hypothesis.
- R5: Check request/response headers for service-level explanations (e.g., x-model-variant, x-quantization). Add logging on route selection.

Quick notes from Jon (slack): "saw similar with dedupe pipeline adding suffix for certain route types" — check INF-1423 ticket. Priya suggested looking at recent rollout flags for streaming buffering.

Immediate steps I will take (next 24h):
- Run R1 and R3 against 20 prompts each (overnight job). Save outputs to a temp bucket (note: must not include customer data).
- Ping infra on whether a post-processing guard was enabled 2026-03-01 (cc: @InfraOps).
- Add a short automated check to test harness: ensure 'closing bracket followed by EOF' pattern for JSON outputs; fail early in CI for rolling deploys.

Lingering questions / TODOs:
- Is there a recent change to the assistant/system prompt for the variant we route to under load? (Who owns route config?)
- If it's post-processing, why did we not see it in staging? Maybe routing differs between staging and hosted prod.
- Are we seeing same delta on Dedicated customers (they might pin older artifacts)? (Customer data case sensitivity)

Random observations:
- The extra commentary tends to be short, sometimes only 6-10 tokens ("Also note:"). That feels like deterministic postpend rather than model hallucination.
- Dropped fields appear more on short extraction tasks (P4), less on long structured responses (P1).

Notes-to-self: capture raw streaming chunks next run (do not re-render). Save both token-level logs and the final assembled string. Keep experiments reproducible: include seed, decoding params, route headers.

If this turns out to be a model artifact, next steps: run a small eval sweep across 10K synthetic extractions to estimate customer impact and consider rollback or soft-fallback to v2.3 for extraction routes. If it's infra/post-process, rollback the microservice change for prod and run a canary to confirm.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after R1/R3 runs.

-- Aisha
